title: Efficient Topic Extraction via Graph-Based Labeling: A Lightweight Alternative to Deep Models
subcategory: automatic topic labelling with embeddings and a knowledge graph
task: Assigning short labels to topic-word lists
problem: Topic-word lists lack clear interpretability, and recent labelling methods rely on expensive LLMs.
architecture: Topic words are concatenated into one sequence and embedded; Direct Similarity Labeling (DSL) picks the topic word whose embedding is closest to the topic embedding; Graph-Enhanced Labeling (GEL) expands the words through ConceptNet into a connected graph and picks the node most similar to the topic embedding; seven sub-400M sentence encoders compared.
llm_or_encoder: all-MiniLM-L6/L12-v2, all-mpnet-base-v2, gtr-t5-large, GIST embeddings; ChatGPT-3.5 and BART-TL as comparisons

datasets.name: Topic_Bhatia
datasets.details: 228 topics with 19 candidate labels each; refined to 219 topics and 1,156 topic-label pairs

datasets.name: 20 Newsgroups
datasets.details: 20 topics, each with label and 10 representative words

key_results: Topic_Bhatia: BERTScore F1 0.955 for DSL (all-MiniLM-L6-v2) and GEL (gtr-t5-large) vs 0.936 for Top2Label.
20 Newsgroups: GEL cosine 0.627 (GIST-all-MiniLM-L6-v2), 0.028 below ChatGPT-3.5 (0.655), vs 0.310 for BART-TL-all.
strengths: Works only from topic words, without reprocessing the corpus, using small encoders.
Close to ChatGPT-3.5 quality at much lower cost.

limitations.text: Evaluation relies on embedding-based similarity (BERTScore, cosine) rather than human judgement; multiple references inflate BERTScore.
DSL can only return one of the input topic words; GEL depends on ConceptNet coverage.
